claim: omniseek_transcribe recovers a distinctive spoken sentence about a script's migration from The Life of Letters episode 'Endangered Alphabets and What Happens When You Write By Hand' at ~16:16; the show ships no transcript and the sentence is not indexed.

ground_truth.value: the script itself was born in India and it migrated eastward

verification.evidence_snippet: And it's associated with Shiingon Buddhism, the script itself was born in India and it migrated eastward and wound up in Japan

search_resistance_prefilter.query: "the script itself was born in India and it migrated eastward"
"the script itself was born in India and it migrated eastward" "Endangered Alphabets"

notes: The phrase straddles two VAD segments (76.42s 'and it migrated' / 81.55s 'Eastward and wound up in Japan'); it is contiguous only in the flat transcript, so containment must be evaluated against the flat transcript. Timestamp is the first segment's start. Only stable-spelling proper nouns (India) are inside the ground-truth string; the ASR-unstable script name (Siddham rendered 'Sidam'/'Siidam') and 'Shingon' were deliberately excluded. Descriptive history of a writing system, not a religious claim.
